So it's a register of all criminal reports and official reports submitted by the crime prevention service to the competent prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, At which moment in time is there an entry made in the KU register?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the day when the report is submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that on the day the report is submitted to the public prosecutor's office, on that same day it is entered into the register; did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because on that day we know exactly what documents we are submitting to the prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I see the time. I don't know if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, you have another six minutes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us then go back to the document first. Thank you for your explanation. Sir, on page 4 we see the contribution of Ratko Jovicic, the chief of the crime prevention service in Zvornik. He states that because of the lack of communication they would send their reports to Bijeljina. He also highlighted the problem of various paramilitary formations and sought help to resolve this problem. Do you remember this person and his contribution to the discussion?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the first time that I saw this gentleman, on that day. Although Zvornik was part of the Security Services Centre Sarajevo Romanija-Birac, we had never received any information from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what paramilitary formations were highlighted by this gentleman and sought help in order to resolve the problems related to them?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the same page, at the beginning of this page, we see the contribution of Nikola Milanovic. You said that he was an inspector of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska. In the last sentence he says, he, that is, Milanovic, emphasised the need to resolve the problem of judicial organs and detention facilities. He also emphasised the need to observe persons of Serbian ethnicity who committed crimes against civilian population. Do you remember these words by Inspector Milanovic?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, could you just read all that again very slowly, please, Mr. Zecevic, because the English translation doesn't -- that we got over the earphones doesn't bear much relation to what's in the English translation on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to read from the Serbian original: Nikola Milanovic from the Serbian MUP from the crime prevention administration emphasised that in the cases where detention, where people are taken into custody, it is mandatory to issue appropriate documents. Then he highlighted the need to resolve the issue of judicial organs as soon as possible, as well as the situation related to prisons and detention facilities. After that, he emphasised the need to deal with the persons of Serb ethnicity who commit crimes against civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think this is one of our translations and I think it may have to go back because "deal with" and "observing" as well as some of the other matters that Mr. Zecevic read out is not quite what appears there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the last thing in relation to this document that I'm interested in are the conclusions on the last page, where we find conclusion number 6: "Maximal engagement of all the operational workers for documenting war crimes and submitting criminal reports against known and unknown perpetrators ..." Do you remember this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I was the person who wrote up the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this meeting, this report and the conclusions, was any action taken in the subsequent period, after the 28th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crime prevention service, depending on the way it was organised in public security stations, began working in a more concentrated way in relation to all the issues related to crime, including this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "this," are you referring to the period after July 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before the witness resumes the stand, we have a brief oral ruling to deliver. The Trial Chamber is seized of a Stanisic motion filed on the 14th of June to amend its Rule 65 ter exhibit -- list of exhibits by adding 41 documents which are intended for use with the witness currently on the stand. The Trial Chamber notes the submissions made orally by the parties earlier in court. The Prosecution does not object to the addition of 17 of them: 924D1, 925D1, 928D1, 929D1, 933D1, 936D1, 949D1, 953D1 to 961D1. And also 927D1, in relation to which the Prosecution merely highlights the apparent duplicity with a document admitted in court yesterday as 1D575. The Prosecution objects to the remaining documents, arguing that seven are not relevant as they concern municipalities outside the indictment, that is, 923D1, 926D1, 931D1, 932D1, 934D1, 937D1, 951D1. And four are not sufficiently important, namely 922D1, 930D1, 935D1, and 950D1. Two documents, 962D1 and 932D1, have already been tendered and admitted as 1D576 and 1D578, respectively. The motion is therefore moot in this respect. The Chamber further notes the submissions and reply made by the Defence in relation to the individual documents. All documents for which translations have been provided fall within the temporal scope of the indictment and relate to matters relevant to the functioning of RS MUP, including policies, structure, and communications. The Trial Chamber is thus satisfied that they are all prima facie relevant, probative, and of sufficient importance so as to justify their late addition on to the Stanisic's Rule 65 ter Exhibit list. Nine of these documents, 953D1 to 961D1, were only disclosed to the Defence on the 8th of June. And thus the Defence has shown good cause for its request to add them to its Rule 65 ter list. With regard to the other documents, the Trial Chamber notes the Defence submission that it only discovered them last week on the electronic disclosure system, stating that prior searches using the same parameters have not been successful. Due to the nature and shortness of these documents and the fact that the Prosecution will not start its cross-examination until next week, the Trial Chamber is satisfied that no undue prejudice arises from granting the request. For these reasons, and in the interests of justice, the Chamber allows the addition of the translated documents to the Rule 65 ter list of the Stanisic Defence. The Trial Chamber remains seized of the motion with regard to the 12 documents which are not yet translated. Could we have the witness back on the stand, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I, before the witness starts, just mention something. I've just received an e-mail pointing out that before Your Honours came in the microphones all apparently were working in court so that people outside the court could hear what was being said. As it so happens, we were having a discussion about the legal merits of part of the indictment. But could I just ask, please, that we make sure that everything is switched off when the court's not in session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tusevljak --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have P1061. It's tab 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, this document is dated the 28th of July, 1992. It's signed by the chief of the Security Services Centre, Zoran Cvijetic. The document was sent to the public security stations, more specifically, their chiefs. The document is already in evidence so I will only need you to comment on one issue related to it. On page 2 of this document, and this is a document transmitting an order by the minister of the interior of the 27th of July related to disbanding of special units. And it goes on to say, in the second passage from the top on page 2, and it's at the very bottom of the English page: "This order also reiterates that individuals who have criminal responsibility for criminal offences prosecuted ex officio (except political and verbal misdemeanours) as well as persons who during the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina committed crimes and against whom no criminal proceedings have been instituted should be removed from the Ministry of the Interior." Do you remember this order by the minister of the interior that all individuals who had criminal records should be removed from the ministry, that is to say, persons who do not rise to the standards of the Ministry of the Interior as well as the persons who committed crimes? Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the last sentence it says: "Persons who during the war in the territory of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina committed criminal offences and against whom for known reasons no proceedings had been instituted." Do you know what does it mean, "for known reasons"? What reasons are they?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is precisely the non-existence of courts and prosecutor's offices in certain areas under jurisdiction of certain police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean the same thing that we saw in the previous case, that criminal reports are submitted -- were submitted when judicial organs were established, or does it mean something else?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that when the appropriate judicial organs are established, then it can be done, because they had not existed before, so it was not possible to submit the criminal reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry, before Mr. Zecevic leaves the document, in the original, which doesn't show up on the screen, where you can see the highlighting or the marking by that particular paragraph, something is written, and it may be in the copy that Mr. Tusevljak has. I'd like him to read it out and tell us, please, what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, on the second page of this document, on the left-hand side of the page, we see some handwriting and some lines. Could you read out what it says here, if it's possible to read it out.

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 2 I see the word "Pantic." And I can explain this, why we see Pantic written here. We can see from this dispatch that it was taken from a public security station in Milici. We can see that from the first page. Take a look at the stamp. You can also see that Milici is also underlined. This was most probably written by the then chief of the public security station, Zvonko --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter did not hear the last name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because Pantic was the commander of the station in Milici at the time. So this was not part of the original dispatch. This is the copy of the person who received the dispatch and that person wrote this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just one thing. The interpreters could not hear one thing. We see "Zvonko" in transcript. You said: "This was ... probably written by the ... chief of the ... station ..." Could you repeat once again: To whom was this sent and who was the commander of the station in Milici?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the police station was Rade Bjelanovic. While komandir of this station was a person called Pantic, whose first name I cannot recall right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was Rade Bjelanovic the chief of the public security station in Milici?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And Pantic was the commander, komandir; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does this satisfy, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. That's very helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, now that we are talking about the members of the Ministry of the Interior that committed criminal offences, in those cases when members of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska committed criminal offences, were they treated in the same manner as all other persons or were they treated differently?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were treated in the same manner as all other persons. But besides filing an official report against them, there would also be disciplinary proceedings, which means that they would be removed from the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, was there any distinction made - and I'm talking here about the disciplinary proceedings - depending on whether the criminal offence or grave breach of work duty was committed against a non-Serb victim as opposed to the situation when the victims of criminal offences or those grave breaches were of Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They received the same treatment regardless of the victim of the criminal offence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you sure about this?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, why wouldn't I be? The law was the same for everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the beginning of today's session we spoke about the removal of the chief of the public security station in Vogosca and the criminal report submitted against him, as well as the replacement of some other managerial staff in that public security station, because the station did not carry out their tasks and duties in accordance with the Law on Internal Affairs. Were there such cases in some other stations in the territory covered by the Security Services Centre Sarajevo Romanija-Birac?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in 1992 the entire management of the public security station in Pale was also replaced. I also believe that there were some other personnel changes in police stations. I believe Sokolac may have been one such station. But chiefs and commanders were being replaced all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, reasons for replacement or removal of top personnel in public security stations, what were they actually?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: These decisions were made only by the then chief of the CSB Zoran Cvijetic. And he, on the basis of the reports he received and the assessments made, dismissed these persons because they were not carrying out their duties in accordance with the Law on the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And if there were elements of crime involved in what they had done, what would happen then?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where criminal liability was established, then a criminal report was filed with the office of the prosecutor and they were held accountable.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, you mentioned the public security station in Pale, what about the members of this police station in Pale, were disciplinary proceedings instituted against any one of them or were criminal reports filed against any of the top personnel from the Pale Police Station?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, a criminal report was filed against the chief of the administrative and legal department in that police station and his employees because of some of the things they did in relation to issuing public -- personnel documents and the like.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember his name perhaps? His last name?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right now I don't seem to remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that the entire top personnel of the public security station of Pale was replaced at one point in time in 1992. Do you remember who the chief of the public security stations of Pale was basically throughout 1992 or, rather, from April until October?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Malko Koroman was the chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was Malko Koroman replaced?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether that had been requested earlier on as well, whether there were requests for his removal even before the end of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the chief of the CSB had asked for him to be removed even earlier than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to that request of the chief of the CSB?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that first time the citizens did not allow that to happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry, I think we really need to establish the basis for this line because at the moment he's saying "I think," "I don't know," and whether he has any basis in anything he was told at the time or saw at the time. At the moment it seems to be nothing but guess-work.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, the public security station in Pale, did it belong to the CSB Sarajevo Romanija-Birac?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At collegium meetings of the CSB were you usually present, along with other top personnel?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether there was mention at any one of these collegium meetings of problems or the situation at the public security station in Pale?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we received quite a bit of information regarding the situation in the public security station in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What did this information indicate, the information that you received?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It indicated how the Pale Public Security Station was working and what the problems there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What about the chief of the CSB or other top personnel, did they make any comments on the work of the public security station in Pale and its chief?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, comments were made with regard to the work of that public security station and its chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At these meetings, including the late Chief Zoran Cvijetic, did anyone say anything or mention anything, any kind of measures that had to be taken in this regard or that he intended to take in this regard?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief Zoran Cvijetic insisted in the Ministry of the Interior that the chief in Pale be replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: How come you know that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present, myself, when Mr. Zoran Cvijetic asked for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Who from the ministry was asked?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The top personnel of the Ministry of the Interior, so it's probably the minister or one of his assistants.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you say that they were there together with him. Were you present or ... or ... or what?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic talked to me personally about that and he said that he insisted on his removal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And how do you know that he talked to someone from the top echelons of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he told me so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And from whom did you receive that information that you told us about at the very beginning, namely that citizens prevented the removal of Malko Koroman the first time?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who I received that information from. But it was generally known that citizens had assembled around the station and prevented his removal. It was generally known. It was probably in the media or someone from the police or some citizens said so. It doesn't matter, it was a generally-known thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened with Mr. Malko Koroman after he was replaced?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he got a lower position at the public security station in Foca as an inspector or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether other top personnel from the public security station of Pale were removed as such?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this chief of the administrative and legal department was replaced on that occasion. And now I cannot remember whether the komandir was replaced as well, but I think that someone did replace him as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise, like yesterday we have a problem with the map. I've just been informed by the Registry that the map that you drew, 1D580, tab 146, due to certain electronic difficulties in this computer programme, was not saved.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D580. Could that please be shown to you once again. 65 ter 10133, Prosecution. Tab 146.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And could the usher please give you a marker so that you could once again underline those public security stations that belong to the CSB Sarajevo. I am sorry. Perhaps it's better if we take a blue marker this time.

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would really like to ask that this eastern part be zoomed in, enlarged, because you can barely see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Fantastic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, would it not -- may I make a suggestion: Would it not be quicker if simply this was an exercise he did outside court rather than going through all of this again and it can be then admitted by us. In fact, in a proper map, all the police -- all the SJBs are clear as to where they all are.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But what I want to show is the vast territory that it covers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand that. But why not simply give him a map which he can take back with him, mark it, and bring it back and we'll have it admitted as an exhibit. This is going to take forever otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't have a problem. If the Trial Chamber is satisfied with that, I can provide my map and then give it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, provided that the -- as long as the witness has a copy with which he can work. I suppose we'll have to forego any advantage of having an electronic version of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, it seems to me I'm not quite clear about this -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Ms. Korner, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We'll make an admission as to where these places are. They're all set out here in the chart, in any event. They can all -- anybody getting a map can see where these places are. I'm not at all clear why we need to spend time on this exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, but instead of having this conversation, we already could have had the witness mark the map and we move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] We couldn't because it takes him forever.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, it doesn't, Ms. Korner, it takes three minutes. I gave the reasons why I think it's important and in due time I will make submissions on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please, just underline them. You don't have to tell us anything now; we already have it in the transcript. We have all the public security stations. So just underline them so we have this saved and let's move on.

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This should be now Exhibit 1D580.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tusevljak, could you please take a look at tab 152.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope we haven't lost this again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] We have it. You misinterpreted the nod.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P730, tab 152.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document dated the 3rd of August, 1992, addressed to the Ministry of the Interior to the minister, report on the realisation of the order number 10/17/92, dated the 27th of July, 1992. And it says: "Acting in accordance with your order, number as above, and in accordance with the working agreement with the Romanija-Birac Security Services Centre chief, I visited the majority of the public security stations in that area except for Skelani and Bratunac, which were visited, as agreed, by chief of the police department in CSB, Drago Borovcanin." We only have six pages of this document. It is incomplete and it is not signed. Can you tell us who is the author of this document, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the heading of this document, one can see that the author of the document is someone from the administration for the police duties and affairs of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 6 of this document under (a) to (g) we can see these points and then the penultimate paragraph that begins with: "There are obvious problems with information transmission from the SJB level to the MUP level, in all lines of work. The system of communications is broken, the telephones are not working, the faxes are out of order, there are risk areas that are often disrupted, et cetera." Is this, as noted in the report, in agreement with what you know about the issues from the period in question?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I absolutely agree with this because I said awhile ago that we had difficulties in communicating with the police stations at the level of the Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document I wish to show you is P993. It is tab 18. This is a document from the Sarajevo CSB, that's the Romanija-Birac one. It's a report about performed supervision of the state of the organisation and the work of the Bratunac and Skelani police stations. It says that the supervision was performed from the 1st of August until the 3rd of August and that it was performed by Drago Borovcanin and Kojo Vucicevic. So in accordance with the previous document, what I'm interested in is the following; on page 2 in the sixth paragraph, talking about the Skelani Public Security Stations, it says: "By a decision of the minister of the interior, Stevanovic, Bogdan was assigned komandir, and Vasiljevic, Milos as his deputy. At the same time, the local municipal organs without the agreement of the ministry appointed Slavoljub Simic as commander and Ostoja Bozic as his deputy. After a short period of time, Simic left the service on his own free will and he assigned all of the duties and the administration to his deputy Bozic, who completely ignored commander Stevanovic and his deputy, who were legally appointed by the ministry." Mr. Tusevljak, did you know anything about this situation in Skelani?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as Drago Borovcanin was the chief, he was the chief of the police department at the collegium. When he returned from this trip, he informed the chief of the CSB, and I attended this collegium meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you have such or similar situations in the territory covered by the CSB in other places except for Skelani?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is already the third police station that we are talking about which had the same or similar kind of problems. I think that there were such problems also at the Rajlovac Public Security Station because from the beginning it was not known who was the komandir, who was the chief, who was appointed and who wasn't. I also wish to note that, now that we are talking about Skelani, I think that this problem was only resolved in January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us please look at 1D188, which is tab 20. It's a report on measures, crime prevention measures, on the territory of the centre. This document has three pages. It is not signed. It's not even stated which centre is this, which centre does it refer to. Can you tell us something about this document? Are you familiar with it? Do you know who the author is and what it refers to?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document produced by my service. It is an internal one. And it was probably submitted to the chief of the centre, that is to say, the analysis service, so that a compiled report could be made about the activities of the centre and the services.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this amalgamated report, who was it submitted to?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The amalgamated report is submitted to the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will now show you another document, and I would like you to comment on the connection between the document which I'm about to show you with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please show the witness P992. That is tab 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 30th of July, 1992. It was sent to the public security stations on behalf of the crime prevention department of the Sarajevo CSB. I apologise. On behalf of the Crime Prevention Department Sarajevo. It is signed by Chief Simo Tusevljak. Tell me, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is that your signature? Is that your document?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I see that the subject is "Forwarding information," and the text then states what information that is. Why did you need this information in the period between the 1st of April and the 30th of July?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely in order to draw up the complete report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, this forwarding of information, as it refers to the period between the 1st of April and the 30th of July, 1992, was that the first request made in 1992 for information to be forwarded or submitted to the local public security station and sent by the Security Services Centre?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the information that was submitted, was that the basis on which the previous document we looked at was drawn up? It was 1D--

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the counsel please repeat the name of the -- the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, the interpreters ask that you repeat the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: My question was: Was this the basis -- the information that was submitted to you, was that the basis for drawing up the document which we saw earlier, which is marked as 1D188, tab 20?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did this report - I'm talking about the document 1D188, tab 20 - represent the first complete report sent by the Security Services Centre in dealing with the situation with regard to crime which was submitted to the MUP in the year 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There is no date here in this document, but when you look at it can you tell us approximately what was the date or the month when this report was drawn up and submitted to the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document, tab 20, which I have here before me, was submitted to the chief of the centre or the analysis department which then, on the basis of this document, wrote a report on the work of the entire centre, not just with regard to duties relating to crimes but also other duties that the centre discharged. So this was submitted within the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: My question was whether you could tell us, as the document has no date, when this was, in which month in 1992, when you submitted this document to the centre so that they would then draw up the complete report for the ministry.

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can see from this document that it was most probably drawn around the 15th of August, 1992, or immediately thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let me give Mr. Zecevic and the witness a hand. If you look at the report - which you've got the wrong one up on the screen - you will see on page 3 it talks about receiving a memo on the 25th of August. So it must have been sometime after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Ms. Korner for the intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. Just one more question because we have three or four minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see 929D1. It is tab 154.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document dated the 9th of August. It is signed by the chief of CSB Zoran Cvijetic, and it was submitted to the chiefs of public security stations which are subordinated to the centre, or which belong to it. And it informs them about a document of the Ministry of the Interior of the 7th of August, 1995 [as interpreted], that the official IDs of the Doboj CSB are temporary by nature and that they are currently being replaced by new ones and that their display and use is irregular, that they must be taken away and destroyed. Do you remember this report?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was also discussed at the level of the centre. And this is just one. There must be other such reports for the reason that there was still no official ID of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska in use and then many station chiefs, of their own initiative, produced official IDs and distributed them to their police staff who then used these. I think that this is the date when the rules had already been adopted which defined the design and use of the official IDs of the members of the ministry and we who had received those IDs could show them to the citizens who could then know that we were really members of this ministry. And there were many who falsely identified themselves and produced forged or false official IDs. It's obvious that at the ministry this problem with the false IDs was identified. It was identified that something that existed in Doboj. And, therefore, the order was that at check-points the policemen and crime prevention employees should take away such IDs, from persons who would show them, and be destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me whether you know whether there were any cases when someone broke into police stations in the territory of your CSB or some other CSBs in the territory of Republika Srpska from which such or similar official documents were stolen?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the beginning, at the very beginning of the war, when some other units broke into some police stations rather than members of the ministry themselves, they also took away passports, driving licences, personal IDs, all other documents for citizens which were not fulled out but were just blank forms.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If there are no objections, I would tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, help us out: What's the relevance?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours will remember --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Not with the witness listening.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay, may the witness take the headphones off. Your Honours will remember that during the testimony of MS-001 he testified that on a number of occasions in certain police stations in the territory of CSB Doboj there has been cases of stolen cards and I'm just -- and that he informed -- yes, but Your Honours, the point of the matter is that it is obvious that at that time the situation was such that you would have people who were representing themselves as police, members of the Ministry of the Interior, where in fact they were not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But what does the document add to the viva voce evidence already on record?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, this document -- this document shows that the Ministry of Interior has taken the measures to inform all the CSBs about this situation and to take the appropriate measures in taking these documents and destroying these documents, because those are the official -- the official MUP ID, Your Honour, and that -- the holder of that ID does have, by holding that document, does have certain rights which we will discuss with the witness tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we don't object because we're going to be suggesting this has nothing to do with anything other than the Mice, and that's what this is all about, this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: By a majority, Judge Harhoff dissenting, the document is admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D582, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I see the time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, and with that we take the adjournment to tomorrow morning, and we are back in this courtroom.
